text:
sarah-support: FYI opened an escalation for a customer hitting consistent 500s + high tail latency on /v1/generate. customer reports timeout spikes when model is served from canary. Asking for repro bundle and request ids.

raj-eng: can you paste the request id and a short curl we can use to reproduce? also which model they were hitting (full model name)?

sarah-support: customer provided one request id from their logs: req_3a9f2b. They say the SDK retries then 504s. Model string they send in the request: "rwd/llm-1.3-canary". Quote from customer: "first 30s is fine, then we see 500s for a lot of requests for 10-15 minutes".

kyle-sre: filing standard debug run. please run the debug-collector with the request id so we can grab KV cache traces and kernel timings. short command: `ri-debug collect --req req_3a9f2b --out /tmp/dbundle.tar.gz` then upload to the support bucket.

sarah-support: passing that to customer. also asking them to reproduce with a minimal curl so we can hit our infra directly. posted sample below.

sarah-support: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "X-Request-ID: req_3a9f2b" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model": "rwd/llm-1.3-canary", "input":"summarize: short text"}'
```

ops-bot: debug bundle created: s3://redwood-debug/support/req_3a9f2b/dbundle-1712000105.tar.gz (collector metadata attached).

maria-ml: quick read of the bundle shows elevated kernel stalls during attention matmul when the canary binary path is used. The stable model binary (rwd/llm-1.2.1) doesn't show the same stalls. Could be a quantization kernel change in the canary build. Worth repro'ing by pinning to stable.

raj-eng: interesting — can you share the small log excerpt?

maria-ml: ```json
{"ts":"2024-04-01T10:02:31Z","req":"req_3a9f2b","kernel":"attn_matmul_v2","lat_ms":5620,"host":"gpu-03"}
{"ts":"2024-04-01T10:02:36Z","req":"req_3a9f2b","kernel":"attn_matmul_v2","lat_ms":4300,"host":"gpu-03"}
{"ts":"2024-04-01T10:02:40Z","req":"req_3a9f2b","kernel":"attn_matmul_v1","lat_ms":120,"host":"gpu-05"}
```

maria-ml: that pattern -> v2 kernel only used by the canary runtime. My hypothesis: a kernel fallback path on some sequence lengths degenerates. We should repro with the exact input length distribution.

raj-eng: for repro i'll run this locally against canary and stable. small tweak: add trace header to capture full trace.

raj-eng: ```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\n  -H "X-Request-ID: repro_local_1712000160" \\n  -H "X-Debug: 1" \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd/llm-1.3-canary","input":"<repeat to match customer seq len>"}'
```

deploy-bot: canary rollout started 2024-04-01T09:50:00Z -> 10% traffic. last change: quant-kernel v2 enabled for some subshapes.

kyle-sre: if the repro shows the same spike, fallback mitigation options: 1) pin customer to stable model `rwd/llm-1.2.1` via per-customer override; 2) roll canary back to 0% until issue root cause. Which do we prefer short-term?

maria-ml: short-term: pin customer to stable (low blast radius) and throttle canary rollout to 0% while we patch the kernel. After fix we can re-run a targeted canary test with trace sample.

sarah-support: I'll ask the customer to hit the curl with `model: rwd/llm-1.2.1` and `X-Request-ID: req_3a9f2b-pinned`. Also asking them to upload the debug bundle from `ri-debug collect` to s3 path above.

raj-eng: i'll repro locally now with both runtimes and post traces. if i can reproduce i'll attach a small reproduction script and an exact sequence length that triggers the kernel fallback.

deploy-bot: temporary rollout update: setting canary traffic to 0% (change id roll-2024-04-01-09) — will take ~30s to drain.

sarah-support: noted, updating ticket. next steps: 1) ask customer to repro with pinned model + run `ri-debug collect` 2) engineering to repro locally and confirm kernel failure 3) plan patch and targeted canary test. I'll follow up in the ticket with the pinned model instructions. :thumbsup:

kyle-sre: tagging the oncall to monitor for any residual latencies.

maria-ml: if anyone needs the minimal repro i produce, i'll post a tiny python script that loops the exact prompt shape and reports median/99p latencies per kernel.

sarah-support: thanks all — closing the slack thread, will re-open if customer can't reproduce.
